guards.description: Windows process has an elevated administrator token.
Windows 10 or 11 x86-64 is running.
Windows booted in UEFI mode and runtime variables are writable.
The system disk is GPT and not dynamic, pooled, or RAID-backed.
Windows, its ESP, and the target free interval resolve to one unambiguous disk.
The Windows system volume is NTFS and reports a supported shrink range.
The plan leaves Windows MSR and recovery partitions unchanged.
AC is connected or battery policy allows a reboot-spanning install.
No pending Windows servicing restart, feature update, storage repair, or other reboot owner can compete with installer handoffs.
The system disk and NTFS volume report no dirty state, repair requirement, or failing health condition.
Supported NTFS shrink space covers XBOOTLDR, root minimum, and safety margin.
The existing ESP has enough space for the namespaced signed loader.
Secure Boot is off or every loader and UKI signature chains to accepted trust.
The signed journal proves that no installer BootNext rearm has already been attempted.
The signed journal proves no installed-JStack BootNext rearm has already been attempted.
The signed journal proves the single installed-JStack BootNext rearm was already attempted.
The signed journal proves that the single permitted installer BootNext rearm was already attempted.
Canonical metadata, immutable local policy, signature quorum, compatibility bindings, and release lifetime validate before durable acceptance.
Canonical Ed25519 quorum, immutable local policy, channel, architecture, graph digest, protocol, lifetime, and durable anti-rollback acceptance validate.
Durable evidence binds the accepted manifest, acceptance-state hash, and exact promoted artifact set.
The exact byte stream currently being consumed matches every signed chunk hash, whole hash, size, and EOF.
Current disk GUIDs, offsets, sizes, and types match the planned fingerprint.
The current plan hash exactly matches the user-confirmed plan hash.
BitLocker protection is enabled on the Windows system volume.
BitLocker protection is disabled or not applicable.
The user confirmed access to valid BitLocker recovery material.
The registered Windows finalizer has no signed Linux completion token and must dispatch bootstrap recovery instead.
A signed Windows finalizer is registered before cross-OS reboot.
All proposed writes remain inside the confirmed unallocated interval.
The XBOOTLDR GUID, type, offset, and size match the plan before formatting.
The XBOOTLDR GUID, type, offset, size, and filesystem match the plan.
The cross-OS handoff, journal sequence, accepted manifest, and durable staging-evidence hash validate.
The original Windows boot entry and namespaced ESP files remain intact.
Root image, fstab, users, network, Niri, boot artifacts, and recovery units validate.
BitLocker protection is active again or was never enabled.
The signed JStack boot entry resolves to the installed release.
Recovery controller is executing under Windows.
Recovery controller is executing under the RAM installer.
A confirmed mutation exists and recorded JStack resources remain identifiable.
Every rollback target matches an object created by the journaled plan.

actions.description: Collect hardware, firmware, power, BitLocker, disk, partition, and boot inventory.
Compute an immutable plan using supported shrink bounds and stable GUIDs.
Lock the trusted staging root, remove untrusted cache names, and retain syntactically eligible resumable files for mandatory chunk rehash before use.
Compare-and-swap append the anti-rollback acceptance record, flush its commit marker, reopen it, and require exact canonical readback.
Download the signed release and channel manifest.
Verify canonical metadata, immutable trust policy, signature quorum, compatibility bindings, and release lifetime to produce a pending acceptance capability.
Download into no-follow quarantine, retain only complete verified logical chunks, and flush every resumable boundary.
Full-hash quarantined artifacts, durably promote them by digest without clobber, reopen them, and persist exact staging evidence.
Display exact disk identity and before/after layout.
Record explicit confirmation bound to the exact plan hash.
Register the signed reboot finalizer and recovery entry.
Suspend BitLocker protectors with RebootCount 0 only after recovery material and the gated startup dispatcher are durable; explicit finalization or rollback restores protection.
Shrink the Windows partition and NTFS filesystem through the Windows Storage API.
Create the planned XBOOTLDR GPT partition inside confirmed free space.
Format XBOOTLDR as FAT32 with the planned label and GUID.
Open promoted artifacts no-follow and hash the same byte stream copied into a journaled XBOOTLDR destination before committing it.
Open the promoted loader no-follow and hash the exact source stream written under the namespaced ESP path.
Create a UEFI boot entry for the signed JStack installer loader.
Reopen the installer loader and UKI no-follow and verify exact size, chunks, whole hashes, and EOF immediately before setting BootNext.
Set BootNext to the verified installer boot entry.
Request an orderly reboot after the next durable state and resume token are flushed.
Verify handoff, journal chain, accepted manifest, staging-evidence hash, and actor transition.
Re-inventory GPT and require the confirmed plan fingerprint to match.
Create only the planned JStack root partition inside confirmed free space.
Create the planned Btrfs filesystem and subvolume layout.
Open the promoted system image no-follow and hash the exact stream deployed into the uncommitted root destination.
Configure users, locale, Niri, networking, firmware, recovery, and first boot.
Open promoted UKIs no-follow and hash the exact source streams installed on XBOOTLDR.
Mount and verify root, boot artifacts, manifests, and required services.
Set Windows as the next boot and record finalizer mode.
Confirm Windows boot, volume identity, and planned JStack partitions.
Restore BitLocker protection when it was suspended.
Remove transient Windows bootstrap state while preserving recovery metadata.
Set BootNext to the verified installed JStack boot entry.
Verify root, boot, Niri session, networking, and recovery services.
Set Windows as next boot and mark the signed journal for rollback mode.
Remove only boot entries created by this installation plan.
Remove only ESP paths recorded as created by this plan.
Delete only root and XBOOTLDR partitions whose GUIDs match the plan.
Expand Windows into adjacent recovered space through the Windows Storage API.
Remove the signed finalizer task and rollback registration.

invariants.description: Mutations require the exact confirmed plan hash.
Disk identity and layout are revalidated before mutations.
Only Windows Storage APIs shrink or expand NTFS.
Windows boot and recovery resources are never replaced.
BootNext is armed only for a validated trust chain.
Recovery material and finalizer exist before suspension.
Every mutation has intent, pre/postconditions, and recovery policy.
Unexpected disk identity enters manual recovery without writes.
Success requires Windows finalization and JStack first boot.
No transition erases Windows or enters replace-disk mode.
Each action executes only under an actor authorized for that platform.
No competing Windows servicing or repair reboot is pending when installation begins.
Firmware handoff to the installer may be rearmed at most once before rollback.
Rollback mutates only objects whose stable identities were recorded by the confirmed plan.
Each transition contains at most one mutating action so partial progress has a named durable checkpoint.
Planning and payload staging require an exact reopened readback of the monotonic release acceptance record.
Only no-follow, flushed, full-hash-verified artifacts promoted under their signed digest can enter durable staging evidence.
Each privileged consumer hashes the exact source byte stream it copies or deploys before committing the destination.
